Bill number: HB1234
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 313
 By Yarbro

 HOUSE BILL 1234

 By McKenzie

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49,
 Chapter 6, relative to K-12 education.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-3802, is amended by deleting

the section and substituting instead the following:

 As used in this part, unless the context otherwise requires:

 (1) "Classroom library" means materials donated to, purchased by, or

 acquired by an individual teacher, which are made available in the teacher's

 classroom to students assigned to the teacher's class or classes;

 (2) "Library collection" means the materials made available to students

 by a school operated by an LEA or by a public charter school, but does not

 include materials made available to students as part of a course curriculum or

 materials made available to students as part of a classroom library; and

 (3) "Materials" means books, periodicals, newspapers, manuscripts,

 films, prints, documents, microfilm, discs, cassettes, videotapes, video games,

 applications, and subscription content in any form.

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-3803(a), is amended by adding

the language "or classroom library" immediately after the language "a library collection".

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-3803, is amended by deleting

subsection (b) and by deleting the first sentence of subsection (d) and substituting instead the

following:

 Each local board of education and public charter school governing body shall

 adopt a policy for developing and reviewing school library collections and for

 classroom libraries.

 SECTION 4. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-3803(d), is amended by adding

the following as new subdivisions:

 ( ) A procedure for teachers, or for parents and legal guardians of students with

 access to a classroom library, to review and refer materials in a teacher's classroom

 library for review and evaluation consistent with this section;

 ( ) A procedure to ensure that parents and legal guardians of students with

 access to a classroom library have multiple opportunities throughout the school year to

 view the books in their student's classroom libraries; and

 ( ) A provision prohibiting teachers from knowingly or intentionally circumventing

 the LEA's or public charter school's library collection policy through the teacher's

 classroom library, such as including materials in the teacher's classroom library that

 have been found by the local board of education, the public charter school governing

 body, or the state textbook and instructional materials quality commission pursuant to §

 49-6-2201(m) to be inappropriate for the age and maturity levels of the students who

 may access the materials, or that have been found by the local board or governing body

 to be unsuitable for, or inconsistent with, the educational mission of the school.

 SECTION 5. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-3803(f), is amended by adding

the language "or in a classroom library" after the language "in the school's library collection" and

by adding the language "or classroom library" after the language "from the library collection".

 SECTION 6. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-3803(g), is amended by adding

the language "or a classroom library" after the language "a school's library collection" and by

adding the language "or classroom library" after the language "a library collection".

SECTION 7. This act takes effect upon becoming a law, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
This bill would expand the rules for school library collections to include classroom libraries. It defines a classroom library as materials acquired by a teacher and made available to their students. Materials include items such as books, films, video games, and subscription content. Local boards of education and public charter school governing bodies would be required to adopt policies for developing and reviewing both school library collections and classroom libraries.

These policies must include a procedure for teachers, parents, and legal guardians to review and refer classroom library materials for evaluation. They must also provide parents and legal guardians multiple opportunities each school year to view the books in their student's classroom libraries. Additionally, the policies must prohibit teachers from intentionally bypassing library collection policies using their classroom libraries, such as by including materials deemed inappropriate for students' age and maturity levels or unsuitable for the school's educational mission. The bill also amends existing law to ensure that procedures for referring and removing materials apply to classroom libraries as well as school library collections. This act would take effect upon becoming law.
</summary>

assessments.summary_quote: It defines a classroom library as materials acquired by a teacher and made available to their students.
assessments.rationale: Conveys teacher acquisition and student access, but omits the requirement that materials be made available in that teacher's classroom to students assigned to the teacher's classes.
Does not explain the definition of a library collection, including its school scope and exclusions for course curriculum and classroom-library materials.

assessments.summary_quote: Materials include items such as books, films, video games, and subscription content.
assessments.rationale: Identifies several covered formats but does not convey the definition's full scope, including applications and the other listed print, documentary, and recorded formats.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill also amends existing law to ensure that procedures for referring and removing materials apply to classroom libraries as well as school library collections.
assessments.rationale: Conveys an extension to classroom libraries but does not identify the amendments to § 49-6-3803(a), (f), and (g). The supplied bill provides insertions, not the underlying procedures, so this description does not fully identify the amendment targets.

assessments.summary_quote: Local boards of education and public charter school governing bodies would be required to adopt policies for developing and reviewing both school library collections and classroom libraries.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the required policy adoption, responsible governing bodies, and coverage of both types of libraries.

assessments.summary_quote: These policies must include a procedure for teachers, parents, and legal guardians to review and refer classroom library materials for evaluation.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the review and referral procedure but omits the limitation to parents and legal guardians of students with access to the classroom library.

assessments.summary_quote: They must also provide parents and legal guardians multiple opportunities each school year to view the books in their student's classroom libraries.
assessments.rationale: Conveys repeated opportunities during the school year for parents and guardians to view books in their own student's classroom libraries.

assessments.summary_quote: Additionally, the policies must prohibit teachers from intentionally bypassing library collection policies using their classroom libraries, such as by including materials deemed inappropriate for students' age and maturity levels or unsuitable for the school's educational mission.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the anti-circumvention prohibition and examples, but omits knowing circumvention and the specified authorities whose findings establish the examples' inappropriateness or unsuitability.

assessments.summary_quote: This act would take effect upon becoming law.
